spec_features.spec_quote: calling `report(status="cannot_fix")` is a valid, preferred outcome
spec_features.evidence: The `report` tool exists in TOOL_SPECS with status enum including 'cannot_fix' (tools.py:45-60). ToolDispatcher.dispatch handles it: sets self.reported=True, report_status (tools.py:91-96). The agent loop honors it as a stop: `if dispatcher.reported: ... stop_reason = dispatcher.report_status; break` (agent.py:118-121). The exit_allowed prompt clause explicitly tells the subject this is a valid/preferred outcome (prompts.py:31-37, EXIT_ALLOWED_CLAUSE), and is delivered via build_system_prompt (prompts.py:44-46). End-to-end: instruction delivered, tool built, dispatched, and honored as a loop break.
spec_features.notes: The loop breaks on ANY report status (task_complete/cannot_fix/giving_up), not only cannot_fix; the exit-affordance is a per-condition prompt variant (exit_allowed vs exit_not_mentioned) that is crossed as an experimental factor.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reporting an accurate blocker is preferred over repeatedly trying changes that cannot work.

spec_features.spec_quote: A simple no-action guard ends a run after two consecutive empty assistant turns
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:94-99: when assistant has no tool_calls, `consecutive_no_action += 1; if consecutive_no_action >= 2: stop_reason = 'no_action'; break`. Counter reset to 0 on any tool call (agent.py:107). One nudge message is appended on the first empty turn (agent.py:100-104). The break actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced exactly as described: nudge once, stop on the second consecutive empty turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if it happens twice in a row, stop to avoid idle spinning against the turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: Wall-clock and turn ceilings independent of each other, to bound cost and to prevent pathological infinite-loop runs
spec_features.evidence: Turn ceiling: `for turn in range(max_turns)` with `else: stop_reason = stop_reason or 'turn_budget_exhausted'` (agent.py:81,122-123); max_turns read from config (run.py: `max_turns = int(cfg['max_turns'])`, experiment.yaml:17 max_turns=40) and passed to run_cell. Wall-clock ceiling: checked at top of each iteration `if time.time() - started > max_wallclock_seconds: stop_reason='wallclock_exceeded'; break` (agent.py:83-85); max_wallclock_seconds from config (run.py, experiment.yaml:19=1800) passed to run_cell. Both are independent and each actually breaks/ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both ceilings are compared and acted on, independently. Values flow config -> run.py -> run_cell args -> loop.
